messages:
jess: Quick sync — finalizing scale-down / drain behavior for Dedicated GPU pools. My goal: zero-surprise evictions, bounded cold-start cost, and simple operator surface. Proposal below.

matt: sketch it out, what are the invariants?

jess: invariants: 1) never evict active in-flight requests, 2) prefer removing capacity that minimizes global perf regression, 3) respect tenant reserved guarantees, 4) keep small warm buffer for common tenants to avoid tail latency spikes.

rohit: how do we pick which node/pod to remove? cheapest-first? prefer preemptible?

jess: selection order: preemptible nodes -> burst-lane nodes -> pooled shared nodes. Within a class pick node with largest idle time and lowest tenant diversity (fewer pinned tenants). This keeps eviction surface small.

lisa: product question — what will customers see? Will this surface as slower scale-down or as a config?

jess: defaults: conservative scale-down (longer grace) for Enterprise tiers; customers can opt into aggressive reclaim via pool config `scaleDown.aggressiveness`. No visible errors, just slightly slower reclaim.

mike: rough admission pseudocode to capture intent: ```
if pool_util < low_watermark for grace_period:
  mark node DRAINING
  wait until inflight_requests(node) == 0 OR drain_timeout
  if inflight_requests > 0 and tenant_is_high_qps:
    try migrate_kv_cache(tenant) or extend_lease(tenant)
  remove node
```

matt: what is `drain_timeout`? static or dynamic?

jess: dynamic: max(30s, recent_p90_latency * 3, tenant_prewarm_lease) capped at 10m. So for high-latency workloads we allow longer drain.

rohit: cache migration is tricky — can we instead prioritize keeping nodes with heavy prefix caches?

jess: yes — scoring includes `kv_cache_value` per tenant/node; nodes with higher aggregated cache score get eviction penalty. That keeps hot cache colocated.

orch-bot: [test-cluster] drain-simulation failed: scenario "mixed-tenant-burst" produced >0.5% tail latency regression on node removal. CI link: https://ci.example/reports/1234

mike: saw that. Simulation removed node with high cache score by accident — we need to fold cache_score into the selection weight (multiply by 10).

jess: good catch. Also propose a soft-safety: if predicted global tail delta > threshold, abort scale-down and mark pool as "conservative" for next 5m.

lisa: can we expose `predicted_tail_delta` in Console telemetry? PMs want to know why reclaim paused.

jess: yes — Console will show reason (cache-heavy node, high predicted delta, tenant pinned). We'll add an event: `pool.reclaim_blocked` with tags.

rohit: billing question: if we keep warm slots for tenant, who pays?

jess: tenant pays if they have reserved committed capacity. For free/ondemand tenants we absorb a tiny warm buffer as platform optimization; we surface "warm_slot_hours" in billing so customers can see cost.

matt: operator boundary: should this logic live in Dedicated operator or central autoscaler?

mike: keep decision in operator (local view + cache_score) but autoscaler sets global policies & thresholds. Operator reports telemetry and can be overridden by central planner. That keeps latencies tight and control surfaces simple.

jess: agree. Action items: 1) mike - adjust selection weight to include cache_score and tenant_diversity (PR), 2) rohit - billing metric proposal for warm_slot_hours, 3) lisa - UX copy for reclaim pauses, 4) matt - write small RFC that lists math for predicted_tail_delta and dynamic drain_timeout. Meet in 48h to finalize.

mike: I'll open the PR and add sim changes.

jess: thanks — anyone object to this approach?

lisa: no objections from product side. :thumbsup:

rohit: ack.

matt: adding to my queue.

jess: cool — will spin up RFC draft and tag you all. Thanks!"
